slip-on-flange.question: Can slip on flanges be used for Class 900 pressure service?
slip-on-flange.answer: Not recommended — ASME B16.5 limits SO flanges to Class 300 and below for most services. WNRF preferred above Class 300.

slip-on-flange.question: What is the welding procedure for slip on flanges?
slip-on-flange.answer: Two fillet welds required per ASME B31.3 — one at hub face and one at back of flange.

slip-on-flange.question: Do you supply SORF in SS316L?
slip-on-flange.answer: Yes, stocked in Class 150 and 300; higher classes on order.

slip-on-flange.question: What facing finish do you provide?
slip-on-flange.answer: 125–250 AARH serrated finish standard; smooth finish on request.

weld-neck-flange.question: What is the difference between ASME B16.5 and B16.47 weld neck flanges?
weld-neck-flange.answer: B16.5 covers sizes ½" to 24" in classes 150–2500; B16.47 covers 26"–60" in two series (A=MSS SP-44, B=API 605).

weld-neck-flange.question: What pressure class weld neck flange do I need for 600 psi at 400°F in A105?
Do you supply IBR-approved weld neck flanges?
weld-neck-flange.answer: Yes, all our CS/alloy flanges are IBR approved under IBR 1950 regulation 84.

weld-neck-flange.question: What is the lead time for non-standard bore WNRF?
What NDT tests do you perform?
weld-neck-flange.answer: RT, UT, MPT, DPT, hardness, PMI — as per customer specification.

blind-flange.question: What is the maximum pressure rating for a Class 2500 blind flange in A105 at 100°F?
blind-flange.answer: 6170 psi as per ASME B16.5 Table 2-1.1.

blind-flange.question: Can blind flanges be used as spectacle blinds?
blind-flange.answer: No — spectacle blind is a permanent installed assembly with both blind and spacer; blind flange is a separate bolted cover.

blind-flange.question: Do you supply RTJ-faced blind flanges?
blind-flange.answer: Yes, in oval and octagonal ring grooves per ASME B16.20.

blind-flange.question: What is the weight of a 12" Class 600 blind flange in A105?
blind-flange.answer: Approximately 68 kg — contact us for certified weight certificate.

socket-weld-flange.question: What is the socket bore gap required for a socket weld flange?
socket-weld-flange.answer: ASME B31.3 para 328.5.2 requires 1/16" (1.6mm) gap before welding to allow thermal expansion.

socket-weld-flange.question: Can socket weld flanges be used for cryogenic service?
socket-weld-flange.answer: Yes with appropriate material (A182 F304L or F316L) and verified gap procedure.

socket-weld-flange.question: What is the max size for socket weld flanges per ASME B16.5?
socket-weld-flange.answer: 4" NPS is the maximum standardized size.

socket-weld-flange.question: Is one fillet weld sufficient?
socket-weld-flange.answer: One weld is standard; for cyclic or vibration service, double-weld socket per client specification.

threaded-flange.question: What thread standard is used — NPT or BSPT?
threaded-flange.answer: We supply both NPT (ASME B1.20.1) and BSPT (BS 21) — specify at time of order.

threaded-flange.question: Up to what pressure class can threaded flanges be safely used?
threaded-flange.answer: Class 600 per ASME B16.5; above Class 600 a seal weld is mandatory per ASME B31.3.

threaded-flange.question: Can threaded flanges be used for steam service?
threaded-flange.answer: Limited to Class 300 and below for steam; refer to ASME B16.5 temperature-pressure tables.

threaded-flange.question: What is the minimum wall thickness required in the mating pipe?
threaded-flange.answer: Schedule 80 minimum recommended for Class 300 and above.

lap-joint-flange.question: Is the Stub End sold separately from the Lap Joint Flange?
lap-joint-flange.answer: The Stub End and Backing Flange are two separate items — you must order both. When ordering, specify: (1) Backing Flange — size, class, material (usually CS A105); (2) Stub End — size, material (must match pipe), short or long pattern. We can quote as a matched pair.

lap-joint-flange.question: What material should I choose for the backing flange?
lap-joint-flange.answer: Use Carbon Steel A105 for the backing flange in almost all cases — it saves significant cost because the backing flange never contacts the process fluid. Only use an exotic alloy backing flange if the external environment is also corrosive (e.g. seawater splash zone) or if the code requires it (e.g. NACE environments).

lap-joint-flange.question: What is the difference between short pattern and long pattern stub ends?
lap-joint-flange.answer: Short Pattern (per ASME B16.9) has a shorter overall length — adequate for most applications. Long Pattern has a longer straight section, allowing the backing flange to be pulled further back for easier alignment and gasket replacement in tight spaces. Long pattern is used in larger sizes and when spacing is critical.

lap-joint-flange.question: Can Lap Joint Flanges be used in high-pressure service?
lap-joint-flange.answer: Yes. Lap Joint Flanges are available per ASME B16.5 in all pressure classes from 150# to 2500#. However, they are generally not preferred above Class 900# as the lap radius (sealing surface) must resist very high gasket seating stress — Ring Type Joint (RTJ) faces are preferred for critical high-pressure service.

lap-joint-flange.question: Are Lap Joint Flanges the same as Swivel Flanges?
lap-joint-flange.answer: Similar concept. A Swivel Flange is a specific type of backing flange with a machined groove/ring that retains the stub end in position while still allowing rotation — providing more structural rigidity. Standard Lap Joint Flanges simply lap over the stub end with no groove retention. Swivel Flanges are more common in subsea/offshore applications.

long-weld-neck-flange.question: What is the difference between a Long Weld Neck and a standard Weld Neck Flange?
long-weld-neck-flange.answer: A standard WN Flange has a short tapered hub designed to connect to a pipe in a pipeline. A Long WN (LWN) Flange has an extended neck (hub) that acts as the nozzle itself on a pressure vessel, eliminating the need for a separate pipe nipple. The LWN is also bored to a specific pipe schedule to match the connecting pipe exactly.

long-weld-neck-flange.question: Can Long Weld Neck Flanges be custom-bored to any schedule?
long-weld-neck-flange.answer: Yes. The bore of the LWN neck is machined to the exact internal diameter of your connecting pipe. You must specify the pipe schedule (e.g. SCH 40, SCH 80, SCH 160, XXS). We can also provide taper bores for special transition requirements.

long-weld-neck-flange.question: What neck length should I specify?
long-weld-neck-flange.answer: Neck length depends on the vessel wall thickness, insulation thickness, and minimum nozzle projection required by the vessel design code (ASME Sec VIII). As a general guide, neck length = vessel insulation thickness + 100mm minimum clearance. Your process engineer or vessel designer will specify the exact length. We can manufacture to any length.

long-weld-neck-flange.question: Are Long Weld Neck Flanges available in Duplex and Super Duplex?
long-weld-neck-flange.answer: Yes. LWN Flanges are available in A182 F51 (Duplex 2205), A182 F53 (Super Duplex 2507), F55 (Zeron 100), Inconel 625, Hastelloy C276, Incoloy 825, and all other grades in our material table. These are made to order; lead time is 4–8 weeks for special alloys.

long-weld-neck-flange.question: Do Long Weld Neck Flanges require any special inspection?
long-weld-neck-flange.answer: For pressure vessel applications, LWN flanges typically require EN 10204 3.2 MTC (third-party certified), impact testing (if low temperature service), NACE compliance (if sour service), and PMI (Positive Material Identification). We provide all of these on request.

spectacle-blind-flange.question: What is the difference between a spectacle blind and a paddle blank?
spectacle-blind-flange.answer: A spectacle blind is a single-piece figure-8 with both blind disc and spacer connected; a paddle blank (paddle blind) is a separate disc inserted between flanges without the spacer.

spectacle-blind-flange.question: What standard governs spectacle blind dimensions?
spectacle-blind-flange.answer: ASME B16.48 — covers Class 150 to 2500 in sizes 1/2" to 24".

spectacle-blind-flange.question: Can a spectacle blind be used for permanent isolation?
spectacle-blind-flange.answer: It is designed for temporary isolation during maintenance; for permanent isolation, a blind flange is preferred.

spectacle-blind-flange.question: Do you supply in duplex SS F51?
spectacle-blind-flange.answer: Yes — F51 spec blinds available for sour and chloride-rich environments.

mumbai.question: Do you deliver flanges to Mumbai within 48 hours?
mumbai.answer: Standard delivery is 3–5 working days; express 48-hr delivery available for stocked items.

mumbai.question: Can you supply IBR-approved flanges for Mumbai power plants?
mumbai.answer: Yes — IBR certificates provided for all carbon steel and alloy flanges.

mumbai.question: Do you have a Mumbai warehouse or office?
mumbai.answer: We operate from our main facility with regular dispatches to Mumbai — contact our Mumbai sales desk at [number].

mumbai.question: What is the minimum order quantity for Mumbai delivery?
mumbai.answer: No minimum order — we supply from 1 pc to bulk container loads.

butt-weld-elbow-fittings.question: What is the difference between LR and SR butt weld elbow?
butt-weld-elbow-fittings.answer: LR (Long Radius) has centerline radius = 1.5 × NPS — lower pressure drop, preferred for most services. SR (Short Radius) has centerline radius = 1.0 × NPS — used where space is limited.

butt-weld-elbow-fittings.question: What standard governs butt weld elbow dimensions?
butt-weld-elbow-fittings.answer: ASME B16.9 for most; MSS SP-43 for light-wall stainless; MSS SP-75 for high-yield (WPHY).

butt-weld-elbow-fittings.question: Do you supply 3D and 5D elbows?
butt-weld-elbow-fittings.answer: Yes — non-standard radius elbows in 3D and 5D to customer drawing.

butt-weld-elbow-fittings.question: What is the max schedule available for 90° LR elbow in 6" NPS A234 WPB?
Are seamless and welded elbows both available?
butt-weld-elbow-fittings.answer: Yes — seamless for smaller sizes up to 12"; ERW/welded for 14" and above.

butt-weld-tee-fittings.question: What is the difference between an equal tee and a reducing tee?
butt-weld-tee-fittings.answer: Equal tee has all three openings the same size (e.g., 6"×6"×6"); reducing tee has a smaller branch (e.g., 6"×6"×4").

butt-weld-tee-fittings.question: What standard governs butt weld tee dimensions?
butt-weld-tee-fittings.answer: ASME B16.9 for standard wrought fittings; MSS SP-75 for high-yield WPHY grades.

butt-weld-tee-fittings.question: Can you supply reducing tee in duplex SS?
butt-weld-tee-fittings.answer: Yes — A815 WP31803 (Duplex 2205) in ASME B16.9.

butt-weld-tee-fittings.question: What is the minimum wall thickness for a tee in high-pressure service?
butt-weld-tee-fittings.answer: Must meet ASME B16.9 minimum wall which equals or exceeds mating pipe schedule.

concentric-reducer.question: When should I use a concentric reducer vs eccentric reducer?
concentric-reducer.answer: Concentric reducers align pipe centerlines — used for vertical pipes and gas lines. Eccentric reducers offset centerlines — flat side UP on pump suction to prevent air entrainment; flat side DOWN on drain lines.

concentric-reducer.question: What is the length of a 6"×4" concentric reducer per ASME B16.9?
Do you supply reducers in Duplex SS 2205?
concentric-reducer.answer: Yes — A815 WP31803 concentric and eccentric reducers available.

concentric-reducer.question: Can you make custom reducers outside B16.9?

eccentric-reducer.question: Why is flat side up preferred for pump suction eccentric reducers?
eccentric-reducer.answer: Flat side up maintains a consistent top-of-pipe level, preventing air pockets that would cause cavitation in centrifugal pumps.

eccentric-reducer.question: What is the length of an 8"×6" eccentric reducer per B16.9?
Can eccentric reducers be used for gas service?
eccentric-reducer.answer: Yes, but concentric reducers are more common for gas — eccentric used where liquid drainage is required.

eccentric-reducer.question: Do you supply eccentric reducers in SCH XXS?

180-elbow.question: What is the difference between a close-pattern and open-pattern 180° elbow?
180-elbow.answer: Close-pattern return bends have the two openings close together (back-to-back); open-pattern has more space between legs for insulation or mechanical access.

180-elbow.question: Is a 180° elbow the same as two 90° elbows?
180-elbow.answer: No — a 180° fitting is one seamless piece with fewer welds; two 90° elbows require a spool piece and two weld joints.

180-elbow.question: Do you supply 180° elbows in SS316L?
180-elbow.answer: Yes — A403 WP316L in ASME B16.9.

180-elbow.question: What is the back-to-face dimension for a 6" LR 180° elbow?

socket-weld-fittings.question: What pressure class socket weld fitting do I need for 2" SCH80 pipe?
socket-weld-fittings.answer: Class 3000# per ASME B16.11 maps to SCH80; for SCH160 use Class 6000#.

socket-weld-fittings.question: What is the size range for socket weld fittings per B16.11?
Do socket weld fittings require a gap before welding?
socket-weld-fittings.answer: Yes — 1/16" (1.6mm) gap per ASME B31.3 para 328.5.2 to allow thermal expansion during welding.

socket-weld-fittings.question: Can socket weld fittings be used for cryogenic service?
socket-weld-fittings.answer: Yes with F304L or F316L material and appropriate WPS.

socket-weld-fittings.question: What is the difference between a coupling and a union in SW fittings?
socket-weld-fittings.answer: A coupling is welded both ends (permanent); a union has a threaded nut allowing disassembly without cutting.

forged-fittings.question: What is the difference between Class 3000 and Class 6000 forged fittings?
forged-fittings.answer: Class 3000 is rated for use with SCH80 pipe; Class 6000 for SCH160 pipe — higher wall = higher pressure capacity.

forged-fittings.question: Are forged fittings stronger than cast fittings?
forged-fittings.answer: Yes — forging aligns grain structure in the direction of stress, eliminating cast porosity and yielding 25–30% higher impact strength.

forged-fittings.question: What is the maximum temperature for A182 F11 forged fittings?
Do you provide NACE MR0175 compliant fittings for sour service?
forged-fittings.answer: Yes — hardness certified per NACE MR0175/ISO 15156.

forged-fittings.question: What export documents do you provide?
forged-fittings.answer: Commercial Invoice, Packing List, COO, MTR (EN 10204 3.1), IBR Certificate, Third-party inspection reports.

socket-weld-elbow-fittings.question: What class socket weld elbow do I need for SCH160 pipe?
What is the socket depth for a 2" Class 3000 SW elbow?
socket-weld-elbow-fittings.answer: Typically 22mm (0.88") per B16.11 — confirm from dimension table.

socket-weld-elbow-fittings.question: Can socket weld elbows be used for high-temperature steam?
socket-weld-elbow-fittings.answer: Yes with appropriate material — A182 F11 for temperatures up to 593°C.

socket-weld-elbow-fittings.question: Do you supply in F51 Duplex for chloride environments?

alloy-steel-pipes.question: What is the maximum operating temperature for P91 alloy steel pipe?
alloy-steel-pipes.answer: 650°C (1200°F) continuous service per ASME B31.1; creep properties govern above 550°C.

alloy-steel-pipes.question: Why is PWHT critical for P91 pipes?
alloy-steel-pipes.answer: P91 requires strict PWHT at 730–780°C; improper PWHT creates Type IV cracking susceptibility at HAZ.

alloy-steel-pipes.question: What is the difference between P11 and P22 alloy steel?
alloy-steel-pipes.answer: P11 = 1.25Cr-0.5Mo (max 550°C); P22 = 2.25Cr-1Mo (max 593°C) — P22 has higher chromium for better oxidation resistance.

alloy-steel-pipes.question: Do you supply P91 pipes with IBR approval?
alloy-steel-pipes.answer: Yes — ASTM A335 P91 pipes supplied with IBR-approved material certificates and hydro-test records.

alloy-steel-pipes.question: What NDT tests are performed on alloy pipes?
alloy-steel-pipes.answer: Hydrostatic test, UT (ultrasonic), PMI, hardness testing, and radiography for heavy wall pipes.

boiler-quality-plate.question: What is the difference between IS 2002 Grade 2 and ASTM A516 Gr70?
boiler-quality-plate.answer: IS 2002 Gr2 has min UTS 440 MPa (equivalent to Gr60); ASTM A516 Gr70 has min UTS 485 MPa and higher yield — A516 Gr70 is the stronger grade.

boiler-quality-plate.question: When is normalizing mandatory for BQ plates?
boiler-quality-plate.answer: Per IS 2002, normalizing is mandatory for plates > 40mm thick; per ASTM A516 when Charpy impact testing is ordered (supplementary requirement S1).

boiler-quality-plate.question: Do you supply IBR-approved boiler quality plates?
boiler-quality-plate.answer: Yes — all BQ plates supplied with IBR-approved material test reports as required under IBR 1950.

boiler-quality-plate.question: What is HIC-tested A516 Gr70 and when is it needed?
boiler-quality-plate.answer: HIC (Hydrogen Induced Cracking) tested plate per NACE TM0284 is required for sour gas service where wet H2S is present.

boiler-quality-plate.question: What maximum thickness do you stock?
boiler-quality-plate.answer: Up to 150mm in IS 2002 and A516 grades.

hardox-plate.question: What is the difference between Hardox 450 and Hardox 500?
hardox-plate.answer: Hardox 450 has 425–475 HBW hardness; Hardox 500 has 470–530 HBW — higher hardness = better wear resistance but slightly less impact toughness.

hardox-plate.question: Does Hardox plate require pre-heating before welding?
hardox-plate.answer: Yes — pre-heat requirement depends on grade and thickness; typically 75°C for Hardox 450 at 20mm; refer to SSAB pre-heat table.

hardox-plate.question: What is the difference between Hardox and generic AR400/AR500 plate?
hardox-plate.answer: Hardox has tighter hardness tolerance (±25 HBW), guaranteed through-thickness hardness, Charpy impact certified at -40°C, and controlled PCM for better weldability.

hardox-plate.question: What is the maximum thickness available for Hardox 450 in India?
hardox-plate.answer: Up to 103mm — confirm availability at time of order.

hardox-plate.question: Can you cut and profile Hardox plates to size?
hardox-plate.answer: Yes — plasma and oxy-fuel cutting available; laser cutting for thinner gauges.

pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.question: What types of pipe fittings does Remax Forge manufacture?
pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.answer: Flanges (WNRF/SORF/BL/THRF/SWRF/Spec Blind), butt weld fittings (elbows/tees/reducers/caps), socket weld fittings (elbows/tees/couplings/unions), forged fittings, pipes, and plates.

pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.question: Which international standards do you manufacture to?
Do you export pipe fittings?
pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.answer: Yes — we export to 40+ countries including UAE, Saudi Arabia, USA, UK, Germany, Singapore, and Australia.

pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.question: What is your minimum order quantity?
pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.answer: No MOQ for standard items; custom/special items may have minimum batch requirements.

pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.question: What third-party inspections do you accept?
pipe-fittings-manufacturer-india.answer: SGS, Bureau Veritas, Lloyd's Register, TUV, Intertek, and client-nominated inspectors.

buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.question: What countries do you export buttweld fittings to?
buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.answer: UAE, Saudi Arabia, USA, UK, Germany, Australia, Singapore, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and 30+ more — full list on request.

buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.question: What export documents do you provide with each shipment?
buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.answer: Commercial Invoice, Packing List, COO, MTR (EN 10204 3.1), Inspection Certificate, EOEC/Form-I, and any special certifications required (IBR, NACE, PED).

buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.question: Can you meet ARAMCO or ADNOC approved material specifications?
buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.answer: Yes — we manufacture to ARAMCO SAES and ADNOC specifications; please provide your MR/PR for review.

buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.question: What is the lead time for export orders?
buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.answer: 3–4 weeks for standard sizes in stock materials; 6–8 weeks for special grades or large quantities.

buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.question: What payment terms do you accept for export?
buttweld-fittings-exporter-india.answer: LC at sight, 30% advance + 70% BL copy, or as mutually agreed.
